title: 行政の進化と革新のための生成AIの調達・利活用に係るガイドライン

policy_extraction.issuing_body: デジタル社会推進会議幹事会 (Executive Committee of the Digital Society Promotion Council; Secretariat: Digital Agency / デジタル庁)
covered_actors: National government ministries and agencies (各府省庁)
Chief AI Officers (AI統括責任者 / CAIO) of each ministry and agency
Government generative AI system planners (企画者)
Government in-house generative AI system developers (開発者)
Government generative AI system providers/operators (提供者)
Government generative AI system users (利用者, indirectly via ministry-level rules)
Contracted generative AI system vendors and service providers (indirectly governed via procurement specifications, contracts, and supervision)
Incorporated administrative agencies (独立行政法人) and designated corporations (指定法人) (expected to align)
Local governments (地方公共団体) (expected to reference as needed)
prohibited_practices: Handling confidential information (要機密情報) in principle when using general-purpose cloud-based generative AI services provided to unspecified users solely under standard terms of service/agreements (except with formal approval under ministry information security policy)
Using government generative AI systems outside the designated purpose and scope of use defined by the provider or ministry rules

policy_extraction.penalties_summary: The guideline does not establish direct statutory civil or criminal penalties. Compliance is enforced through internal administrative oversight (Digital Agency unified project supervision under the Act on the Establishment of the Digital Agency, CAIO governance, and Advisory Board review) and procurement/contractual mechanisms (including vendor remediation duties, service suspension, and audit rights in Annex 4). Annex 2 notes that unauthorized input of retained personal information used for model training may violate the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (個人情報保護法).
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Designated as a Normative standard guideline (DS-920) within Japan's Digital Society Promotion Standard Guidelines suite, superseding the 'Agreement on Business Use of Generative AI such as ChatGPT (v2.1)'. Currently scoped to text-generating AI systems built on LLMs (including text functions of multimodal models), with image/video generation and AI agents deferred for future expansion. Explicitly exempts government information systems handling Specially Designated Secrets (特定秘密), Critical Economic Security Information (重要経済安保情報), classified administrative documents, and sensitive national security or public safety/order information. Adopts a risk-proportionate framework across three procurement models (Type A standard-terms SaaS, Type B SaaS with individual contract, Type C custom development) and includes four operational annexes: High-Risk Assessment Sheet (Annex 1), Model Usage Rules (Annex 2), Procurement Checklist (Annex 3), and Contract Checklist (Annex 4).

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The guideline is dominantly framed around innovation_enablement: it explicitly positions governance rules as 'guardrails for promoting the utilization of generative AI' to advance adoption and risk management as 'two sides of the same coin,' accelerate a virtuous cycle of innovation, modernize public administration, and ensure proportional risk-balanced controls so that even high-risk innovative projects can proceed safely. Innovation enablement edges out fundamental_rights, economic_competitiveness, and consumer_public_safety because those goals are integrated as supporting objectives or risk-boundary conditions within an overarching mission to drive safe, effective public-sector AI adoption. Secondary frames are nonetheless substantive: fundamental_rights anchors the purpose in Japan's Human-Centric AI Society Principles (dignity, diversity and inclusion) and privacy/non-discrimination protections; economic_competitiveness justifies leading-by-example government adoption and public procurement to boost Japan's international AI competitiveness and foster domestic startups; and consumer_public_safety underpins high-risk classifications targeting harms to human life, body, property, and citizen safety. Social_stability (disinformation, political neutrality) and national_security (foreign server jurisdiction concerns) appear only peripherally, and systems handling national security or public order are explicitly excluded from the guideline's scope.

evidence_spans.quote: 生成AI を含むAI の様々なリスクを抑え、安全・安心な環境を確保しつつ、イノベーションを加速する好循環の形成を図っていくこととされ、イノベーション推進のためにも、ガードレールとなるAI 利活用の安全・安心を確保するためのルールが必要とされたところである。
evidence_spans.quote_en: It was decided to form a virtuous cycle that accelerates innovation while curbing various risks of AI, including generative AI, and ensuring a safe and secure environment; to promote innovation as well, rules that serve as guardrails to ensure the safety and security of AI utilization were deemed necessary.

evidence_spans.source_section: Page 14 (3.2 高リスクな生成AI 利活用の考え方)
evidence_spans.quote_en: When utilizing generative AI in operations where negligence could have a serious impact (such as operations that significantly affect citizens' fundamental rights and safety, operations related to sensitive policy areas, operations affecting human life, body, or property, operations requiring qualifications, or operations requiring high explainability), the risk is considered to be high.
